'''''Corylus heterophylla''''', the '''Asian hazel''', is a species of [[hazel]] native to eastern [[Asia]] in northern and central [[China]], [[Korea]], [[Japan]], and southeastern [[Siberia]].<ref name=foc>Flora of China: [http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200006214 ''Corylus heterophylla'']</ref>

== Description ==
It is a [[deciduous]] [[shrub]] or small [[tree]] growing to {{convert|7|m|ft|abbr=on}} tall, with [[plant stem|stems]] up to {{convert|20|cm|0|abbr=on}} thick grey [[Bark (botany)|bark]]. The [[Leaf|leaves]] are rounded, {{convert|4|–|13|cm|frac=4|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|2.5|–|10|cm|0|abbr=on}} broad, with a coarsely double-serrated to somewhat lobed margin and an often truncated apex. The [[flower]]s are [[Anemophily|wind-pollinated]] [[catkin]]s; the [[male]] ([[pollen]]) catkins are pale yellow, {{convert|4|cm|frac=4|abbr=on}} long, while the [[female]] catkins are bright red and only {{convert|1|–|3|mm|frac=16|abbr=on}} long. The [[fruit]] is a [[nut (fruit)|nut]] produced in clusters of 2–6 together; each nut is {{convert|0.7|–|1.5|cm|frac=4|abbr=on}} diameter, partly enclosed in a {{convert|1.5|–|2.5|cm|frac=4|abbr=on}} long, bract-like [[Involucral bract|involucre]] ([[husk]]).<ref name=foc/><ref name=bean1>Bean, W. J. (1976). ''Trees and Shrubs Hardy in the British Isles'' 8th ed., vol. 1. John Murray {{ISBN|0-7195-1790-7}}.</ref>

It is very similar to the closely related [[common hazel]] (''C. avellana'') of Europe and western Asia, differing in the leaves being somewhat more lobed.<ref name=bean1/>

==Uses==
The nut is edible, and is very similar to the common hazel nut; it is cultivated commercially in China.<ref name=foc/>
